details: Federal Reserve policymakers' recent minutes from November 19-20, 2026, indicate a strong likelihood of further interest rate increases. Some officials even suggested larger hikes if inflation remains persistently high. This hawkish stance has significantly impacted the cryptocurrency market, with Bitcoin plunging below $60,000 for the first time since July 2026. The downturn is also attributed to record outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs and a broader risk-off sentiment in financial markets, influenced by major AI-related IPOs diverting capital.
sourceUrl: While direct, non-paywall Reuters links for specific articles can be difficult to obtain instantly, the sentiment and information were widely reported across financial news outlets, with Reuters being cited for dollar and Bitcoin movements.
title: Hawkish Fed Outlook Drives Bitcoin Below $60,000 Amid Market Sell-off

details: Kristalina Georgieva, head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), stated on November 20, 2026, that the surge in demand from Artificial Intelligence (AI) development is a key factor pushing global inflation to an estimated 4.7% this year. She cautioned that this inflationary pressure, coupled with oil price shocks, will require central banks in many economies to implement tighter monetary policies, leading to higher borrowing costs and potentially impacting economic growth globally.
title: IMF Warns AI Demand Fuels Global Inflation, Necessitating Tighter Monetary Policy

details: On November 20, 2026, Olaf Sleijpen, a senior policymaker at the European Central Bank (ECB), issued a warning that a significant run on stablecoins could destabilize financial markets and potentially compel the ECB to re-evaluate its interest rate policy. This concern arises from the risk of stablecoin issuers being forced to liquidate substantial amounts of reserve assets, such as US Treasury securities, during widespread redemptions, thereby impacting broader financial stability and monetary policy transmission.
title: ECB Official Warns Stablecoin Runs Could Force Interest Rate Policy Changes

details: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Deutsche Bundesbank successfully completed a joint pilot project, "Project Simbolon," on November 20, 2026. The initiative tested the use of wholesale Central Bank Digital Currencies (wCBDCs) for settling euro-Singapore dollar trades across their respective digital asset test environments, aiming to enhance the efficiency of international settlements.
title: Germany & Singapore Successfully Pilot Cross-Border Wholesale CBDC
